answer: Because the quartz index resolves every citation against the opal checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the wander audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 239 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 239 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 16 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
